Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a-c) demonstrate diffuse, randomly distributed micronodules throughout the lung parenchyma, which is the hallmark radiographic appearance of miliary tuberculosis. This pattern correlates clinically with systemic symptoms such as prolonged fever and an elevated sedimentation rate, whereas the other options describe distinct patterns (e.g., large nodules, peribronchovascular distribution, or centrilobular nodules) not seen here.
